newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's economy grows 7.7 pct in first half 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chile's economy grows 7.7 pct in first half 1996.

text.p: Chile's economy, one of the most successful in Latin America, grew 7.7 percent in the first of the year compared with 1995, said the Central Bank.
Exports increased 12 percent in the first six months the year, mainly as a result of the increase in shipments of copper -- the country's largest export, said the bank.
The bank's figures showed imports growing 15 percent in the first half against the same period 1995, which represented a slowdown on the 25 percent increase recorded in the second half of last year.

The figures showed the economy was in the process of a "soft landing" with the Central Bank's credit-squeeze succeeding in cooling rapid growth seen last year, said Deputy Finance Minister Manual Marfan.
"It is a process of adjustment in a background of high growth, which I can only descibe as satisfactory," he said.
The Bank jacked up interest rates towards the end of last year to rein in the economy which expanded over eight percent in 1995.
